findings.issue_text: EventManager.ts:119 — destructuring `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` then accessing `.integration` without optional chaining throws TypeError for MeetLocationType bookings with an empty/null destinationCalendar array, killing booking creation instead of falling back to Cal Video

organizations/create.handler.ts:151 — slug condition inverted from `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug }` to `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}`, so billing-disabled orgs get no slug (unreachable) and billing-enabled orgs get both slug and requestedSlug
organizations/create.handler.ts:151 — the slug condition change is unrelated to the PR's stated purpose (scope creep)

EventManager.ts:170 — `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined` writes undefined credentialId for all non-calendar (video) booking references, breaking later credential lookups for updating/cancelling video meetings

googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:256 — tautological ternary in updateEvent: the `find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` only runs when externalCalendarId is falsy, always comparing against undefined, making the destination-calendar fallback dead code so updates target `primary`/undefined

googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:315 — same tautological find in deleteEvent: fallback branch only runs when externalCalendarId is falsy so the comparison never matches, losing the destination-calendar id and deleting from the wrong calendar

packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:159 (plus office365:73 and larkcalendar:128) — these services still use only destinationCalendar[0] while createEvent is now called once per credential, so non-main-host credentials target the main host's externalId: CalDAV silently creates no event (empty filter → Promise.all([])), Office 365/Lark POST to another user's calendar and 404

googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:148 — selectedCalendar matched strictly on `cal.credentialId === credentialId`, so DestinationCalendar rows with null or stale credentialId no longer match and events silently land in `primary` instead of the configured destination calendar

handleNewBooking.ts:1075 — `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is a silent no-op when evt.destinationCalendar is null, dropping non-organizer hosts' destination calendars for COLLECTIVE events — the exact case the PR is meant to fix

handleNewBooking.ts:731 — rewritten loadUsers dynamic-booking branch drops `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` from the Prisma select, leaving user.organization undefined for dynamic bookings and breaking downstream consumers of the org slug

EventManager.ts:520 — in updateAllCalendarEvents, `updateEvent(credential, ...)` is called unconditionally even when credential is undefined (missing from this.calendarCredentials and DB lookup returns nothing or app.slug is null), unlike createAllCalendarEvents which guards with `if (credential)`

handleCancelBooking.ts:418 — recurring-event branch moved inside a `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)` loop while its body already iterates all credentials × all updatedBookings, deleting every recurring event N times and producing N-1 redundant 404/410 API calls

EventManager.ts:378 — in the else branch (destination with no credentialId), `createEvent(c, event)` is called without the third argument, so externalId is undefined and the booking reference is written with `externalCalendarId: undefined`, preventing later updates/deletes from targeting the right calendar

EventManager.ts:378 — the else branch runs once per destination entry and fans out over all matching credentials, so two destinations sharing an integration type (e.g. two Google hosts without credentialId) create duplicate calendar events for the same booking

EventManager.ts:345 and :505 — `prisma.credential.findUnique` issued inside the per-destination/per-reference loop (N+1 query) and the create loop changed from Promise.all to sequential await, serializing calendar API calls on the booking hot path

EventManager.ts — no test coverage for the new multi-destination path (fan-out over multiple destination calendars, credentialId-based calendar selection in createEvent, DB credential fallback); only test change is a webhook fixture flipping destinationCalendar from null to []

goldens.comment: A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.

Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled

The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).

The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.

googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:148 — selectedCalendar matched strictly on `cal.credentialId === credentialId`, so DestinationCalendar rows with null or stale credentialId no longer match and events silently land in `primary` instead of the configured destination calendar

adjudication.rationale: Real regression risk introduced in the diff. In `GoogleCalendarService.createEvent`, the target `calendarId` is now resolved only via `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId;` and then `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`. Previously it used `destinationCalendar?.externalId` directly. If a `DestinationCalendar` entry lacks `credentialId` (null/undefined) or has a non-matching/stale value, `find(...)` returns undefined and the insert falls back to `primary`, silently ignoring the configured destination `externalId`. The diff elsewhere suggests `credentialId` may be absent (e.g., `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` has an explicit `else` branch for destinations without `destination.credentialId`), making this mismatch verifiable from the code paths shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: handleCancelBooking.ts:418 — recurring-event branch moved inside a `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)` loop while its body already iterates all credentials × all updatedBookings, deleting every recurring event N times and producing N-1 redundant 404/410 API calls

adjudication.rationale: In handleCancelBooking.ts the code changed from selecting a single calendar reference via `find(...)` to `filter(...)` and then looping `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)`. The recurring-event deletion branch (`if (bookingToDelete.eventType?.recurringEvent && ... allRemainingBookings)`) is now inside that outer loop, but its body already iterates over *all* user calendar credentials (`bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(..._calendar)`) and over *all* `updatedBookings`, deleting each referenced event. This means if there are multiple `_calendar` references, the same full credential×booking deletion sweep will execute once per reference, causing duplicate deletes and likely redundant 404/410 responses on subsequent attempts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager.ts:378 — in the else branch (destination with no credentialId), `createEvent(c, event)` is called without the third argument, so externalId is undefined and the booking reference is written with `externalCalendarId: undefined`, preventing later updates/deletes from targeting the right calendar

EventManager.ts:378 — the else branch runs once per destination entry and fans out over all matching credentials, so two destinations sharing an integration type (e.g. two Google hosts without credentialId) create duplicate calendar events for the same booking

EventManager.ts:345 and :505 — `prisma.credential.findUnique` issued inside the per-destination/per-reference loop (N+1 query) and the create loop changed from Promise.all to sequential await, serializing calendar API calls on the booking hot path

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents, the new `for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar)` loop performs `await prisma.credential.findUnique(...)` when a credential isn’t found in memory, which can execute once per destination (an N+1 DB query pattern). Similarly, in the update path, `calendarReference` is now an array and the code loops `for (const reference of calendarReference)` and may call `await prisma.credential.findUnique(...)` per reference. Also, the create path now does `await createEvent(...)` inside the destination loop (sequential per destination) instead of batching all creations via a single `Promise.all`, which serializes calendar API calls across destinations/credentials.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager.ts — no test coverage for the new multi-destination path (fan-out over multiple destination calendars, credentialId-based calendar selection in createEvent, DB credential fallback); only test change is a webhook fixture flipping destinationCalendar from null to []

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce substantial new logic (destinationCalendar becomes an array; EventManager fans out over multiple destinations; GoogleCalendarService now selects calendar by credentialId with DB fallback). The only visible test change is an e2e fixture adjustment (destinationCalendar: null -> []). However, the finding claims “no test coverage” for the new path, which is not a directly verifiable defect from the code change itself: the diff doesn’t prove tests don’t exist elsewhere, and lack of newly-added tests is a process/coverage concern rather than a concrete bug/security/correctness issue introduced by the diff.
